summary: Design a dense non-affine source with affine side rows and a decisive reachable test of degree/free-dimension ratio above one quarter.
Compute the width-eight product-series index fraction at large n after sizing the computation; test whether it remains above one quarter.
Identify which low-degree vanishing-ideal elements a relaxation must miss for a barrier; use the pigeonhole relaxation as a test.
Find refutation degree for added constraints in the degree-filtered function ring of a solution set, starting with down-closed sets.
Commit and test an exact F2 threshold-system closure tool, reproducing n≤9 values and archiving static spans separately.
Explain structured two-partition degrees by a quarter-scale upper bound or find a crossing; use a sparse quotient to reach larger cases.
Evaluate expansion lower bounds for two-partition families with expanding second partition; track the width-dependent constant against ceilings.
Once sources arrive, verify generalized-method hypotheses and positive degree bounds for expanding two-partition families at width four and w.
Sharpen random-formula standard-monomial counts using all small-width derived clauses; test whether thinness reaches the model's degree.
Prove non-thinness of actual random-clause closures from quotient-dimension lower bounds, stating the covered cutoff and density ranges.
Read Alekhnovich–Razborov's reduction operator and derive expanding-clause level-size lower bounds to compare with thinness.
Count sets avoiding boundaries of small connected clause sets via positive correlation; derive a non-thinness range inside expansion.
Bound connected-set sums by overlap-graph spanning trees and replace Markov with concentration for a fixed high-probability range.
Determine whether normalized minimal paired-source cores retain full-scope modular rows and whether single-row ceilings apply to those cores.
Test minimal unsatisfiability and private-variable absence in balanced paired cores; compare occurrence numbers with the shared-pin threshold.
Apply the irregular shared-pin count only to unprojected core rows and express its ceiling through their share of incidences.
Find cutoff-derivable F2 affine consequences in selected paired cores and compute the free dimension used for half bounds and branching.
Prove or refute the paired-row symbol conjecture via shifted-row interpolation or a low-degree dual polynomial outside the preferred cube.
Record named premises for conditional claims and flag those whose registered premise has become a working proof.
Screen live paired, counting and block-cover candidates for polynomial-size parity-Frege or simulated parity-resolution refutations.
Read weak-PHP bounded-depth Frege bounds and test counting-family reductions, retaining excess, size, depth and block-size conditions.
Evaluate the cut-rank ceiling on live candidates using row orders and maximum frontier minus parity rank.
Require Sources read and Not examined for Developed checks; preserve previously unexamined parts until examined or explicitly carried forward.
Show framework commits since a build was queued whose subjects resemble its text, with a tested queue-status listing.
Refuse entries whose registered dependencies lack a link to the notebook source entry or an explicit statement that it was read.
Require measured sizing for the next same-program run after exceeding twice its expectation or reaching its timeout.
Require finite-check entries to identify the script assertion or construction guarantee for each tested hypothesis.
Hold commits resembling queued builds until a reviewer report follows the tool's last change.
Keep the first pre-review draft in ignored logs so later checks can replay the actual text reviewers saw.
Profile all turn-start guidance and reduce its registry-reading cost; preserve timed before-and-after evidence.
Require Best outcome during no-bearing runs to match a notebook-declared goal quantity or explicitly close its item; test the missed case.
Reject Record search or next-step text admitting the attempt's coverage by the record was not checked; test the original missed sentence.
Compare next-attempt sentences with the entry's own newly registered claims and print nearest matches after registration.
Log excerpt reads and require a queued-item cycle to read its latest development, rather than relying on status excerpts.
Search next steps by cited claim IDs and source names so bounds on those objects surface beyond matches to the queue item's wording.
When removing a queue item, print earlier Verification gate sentences reporting refused closures; test the repeated-refusal case.
